# How to Use Microsoft Copilot to Boost Your Daily Creativity

> **In short:** Microsoft Copilot is a free AI assistant that lives in your browser, your phone, and (with a paid plan) inside Word, Excel, and Outlook. Six concrete steps get you from signing in to using it for real work today.

We've all stared at a blank document, trying to find the first sentence for an email or project update. Copilot turns that blank page into a conversation — and once you've tried it once, the rest feels much easier.

## Before you start

Here's what you need before the first step, so nothing surprises you at step four.

- **A free Microsoft account** — any Outlook, Hotmail, or Live address works. No paid plan needed for the browser and phone versions.
- **A modern browser** (Edge, Chrome, Safari, or Firefox) on Windows, Mac, or Chromebook, **or** the free "Microsoft Copilot" app on iPhone (iOS 16 or newer) or Android (10 or newer).
- **For Copilot inside Word, Excel, Outlook, or PowerPoint:** a paid subscription — either *Microsoft 365 Copilot* (around $30 USD/month, roughly $45) for business plans, or *Copilot Pro* for individuals (around $20 USD/month, roughly $30). The in-app features won't appear without one.
- **A specific task in mind.** Even a small one — drafting an email, summarizing a recipe, planning a birthday. You'll get better results with a real goal than with a vague "let me try AI."

## Step 1 — Open Copilot in your browser

On your computer, go to **copilot.microsoft.com** and sign in with your Microsoft account. You'll land on a chat-style page: a welcome message at the top and a text box at the bottom labeled "Ask me anything."

💬 Type this to start:
> "Help me write a friendly invitation to a backyard barbecue next Saturday at 2pm."

You'll know it worked when a reply appears within a few seconds and the text box clears, ready for your next question.

## Step 2 — Pick a conversation style that fits your task

Above the text box, you'll see three tone options: **Creative**, **Balanced**, and **Precise**. Click one before you send your message — it changes how Copilot responds.

- **Creative** — best for brainstorming, image prompts, marketing copy, or playful writing.
- **Balanced** — the everyday default. Fine for most tasks.
- **Precise** — best for factual questions, summaries, and tasks where you want a short, direct answer.

💬 Try this:
> Switch to "Creative", then ask: "Give me five theme ideas for a neighbourhood street party."

You'll know it worked when the reply feels noticeably more playful and varied than the default — that's the style taking effect.

## Step 3 — Draft text inside Microsoft Word (paid plan)

Open Word and a blank document. Look at the ribbon (the strip of icons across the top) — you'll see a **Copilot** button with a colorful four-pointed star icon. Click it and a side panel slides in from the right.

💬 Type this into the side panel:
> "Draft a one-paragraph project update for our team based on this document."

You'll know it worked when a suggested draft appears in your document, or a draft shows in the side panel with an **Insert** button you can click to drop it in.

## Step 4 — Summarize a long email in Outlook

Open Outlook (desktop or web). Open a long email, then click the **Copilot** button in the ribbon and choose **Summary** from the suggested actions.

💬 Try this follow-up after the summary:
> "What action do I need to take from this email, and by when?"

You'll know it worked when a 2–3 line summary appears at the top of the email, listing the key points and any deadlines.

## Step 5 — Generate an image for a slide or social post

In any Copilot chat — browser, phone, or Word — type a request that starts with "Generate an image of…" and describe what you want in plain words.

💬 Try this:
> "Generate an image of a sunny backyard with a long table set for a barbecue, in a friendly cartoon style."

You'll know it worked when four image options appear below the chat. Click one to make it larger, then use **Download** to save it or **Copy** to paste it into your slide.

## Step 6 — Use Copilot on your phone

Download the **Microsoft Copilot** app from the App Store or Google Play and sign in with the same Microsoft account. The layout matches the website — text box at the bottom, plus a microphone icon for voice and a plus icon for attachments.

💬 Try this by voice (tap the microphone):
> "Plan a 30-minute workout I can do at home with no equipment."

You'll know it worked when a spoken reply plays back and a written version appears in the chat, ready for you to scroll back to later.

## Common mistakes

- **Mistake: Asking Copilot without signing in.** Without an account, you get fewer daily turns and can't save chats. Fix: Sign in first — even a free Outlook address works.
- **Mistake: Writing vague prompts.** "Help me with email" gets a vague reply. Fix: Add a role and a goal, like *"Act as a friendly event planner. Give me five themes for a kids birthday party."*
- **Mistake: Trusting every fact.** Copilot can confidently get things wrong. Fix: For anything important — medical, legal, financial, technical — double-check with a trusted source before acting.
- **Mistake: Expecting Copilot inside Word for free.** The in-app features only appear with a Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Pro subscription. Fix: Use the free browser and phone versions until you're ready to pay.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Use Copilot on your phone to plan meals from whatever's in the fridge, draft birthday messages, or summarize a long recipe while you cook.
- **At work:** The Word and Outlook features save the most time — drafting replies from a few notes, and pulling action points out of long email threads.
- **Just getting started:** Open copilot.microsoft.com right now and ask it one small thing. That single habit is how most people get comfortable with AI — one small task at a time.
